question: What is the definition of "Compensation" for RP credits under Section 5.1?
answer: For purposes of RP credits under this Section 5.1, “Compensation” has the meaning given such term in the RP, provided that the Committee may, in its discretion, designate additional or different items as Compensation for purposes of this Section 5.1.

question: When does "Compensation" for RP credits under Section 5.1 include the value of restricted stock awards?
answer: Effective with the 2003 performance year (which awards were granted in 2004) and thereafter, “Compensation” for purposes of RP credits under this Section 5.1 shall include the value of restricted stock awards granted to certain Participants in lieu of cash supplemental Annual Incentive Awards.

question: What is credited to a Participant’s RP-Related Account under Section 5.1(b)?
answer: There shall be credited to a Participant’s RP-Related Account for each Plan Year, in accordance with Section 5.3, an amount equal to the excess, if any, of: (x) the Contribution Credits that would have been credited to a Participant’s Defined Benefit Account Balance under the RP for the Plan Year if the Plan’s definition of Compensation was used, the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation was ignored, and the Participant had not elected or been required to defer the receipt of any Compensation pursuant to a Deferral Plan, over (y) the actual Contribution Credits credited to the Participant’s Defined Benefit Account Balance under the RP for the Plan Year.

question: When are no credits made to a Participant’s RP-Related Account under Section 5.1(b)?
answer: No credits shall be made to a Participant’s RP-Related Account pursuant to this Section 5.1(b) for any pay period ending on or after July 1, 2007.

question: What is the benefits formula for a Plan Year under Section 5.1?
answer: The formula of the benefits for a Plan Year under this Section 5.1 shall be determined by the Administrator and applied in a uniform manner for all similarly situated Participants.

question: What additional years of service may certain Participants be deemed to have rendered?
answer: Certain Participants, as determined by the Company in its sole discretion, may be deemed to have rendered five additional Years of Service under the Plan.

question: What happens when a Participant with a special agreement in Section 5.1(d)(i) has not accrued five Years of Service as of July 1, 2007?
answer: The Participant shall be entitled to receive the credit described in Section 5.1(d)(i) for the 2007 Plan Year as if the RP had remained in effect through December 31, 2007, and the Participant were an active participant in the RP through such date.

question: What is the limitation on receiving credits under Section 5.1(d) for the 2008 Plan Year or later?
answer: Regardless of any special agreement described in Section 5.1(d)(i), a Participant shall not be entitled to receive any credit under this Section 5.1 for the 2008 Plan Year or later.

question: What is the definition of "Compensation" for RSP credits under Section 5.2(a)(i)?
answer: For purposes of RSP credits under this Section 5.2, “Compensation” has the meaning given the term “Total Pay” in the RSP, provided that the Committee may, in its discretion, designate additional or different items as Compensation for purposes of this Section 5.2.

question: When does "Compensation" for RSP credits under Section 5.2 include the value of restricted stock awards?
answer: Effective July 1, 2007, “Compensation” for purposes of RSP credits under this Section 5.2 shall include the value of restricted stock awards granted to certain Participants in lieu of cash Annual Incentive Awards, subject to the limitation set forth in Section 5.2(a)(ii).

question: What is the limitation on Incentive Pay for a Participant in Band 50 or above under Section 5.2(a)(ii)?
answer: “Compensation” of a Participant who is in Band 50 or above for purposes of RSP credits under this Section 5.2 shall not include any Incentive Pay (including the value of any restricted stock awards granted to certain Participants in lieu of cash Annual Incentive Awards) in excess of one times his or her Base Salary.

question: When is the pay band and Base Salary determined for purposes of Section 5.2(a)(ii)?
answer: A Participant’s pay band and Base Salary shall be determined as of January 1 of each Plan Year (or, if the Participant was not employed as an Eligible Employee on January 1, the date the Participant becomes or is rehired as an Eligible Employee, and in the case of a Participant who terminates employment and is rehired as an Eligible Employee within the same Plan Year, the application of this rule shall be determined by pay band as of the date of rehire as an Eligible Employee with respect to Company contributions other than those accrued (and as to which the Participant had met all the prerequisites for receipt) prior to rehire).

question: What is disregarded in determining the Compensation of a Participant for purposes of Section 5.2?
answer: In determining the Compensation of a Participant for purposes of this Section 5.2, “Total Pay” under the RSP shall be determined by disregarding the temporary salary reductions in effect for the pay period commencing March 30, 2009 through the pay period ending on January 3, 2010.

question: What is credited to a Participant’s RSP-Related Account under Section 5.2(b)(i)?
answer: An amount equal to: (A) one percent of the sum of: (1) the Participant’s Compensation, calculated without the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation or Section 415 Limitations, plus (2) that portion of a Participant’s Compensation deferred during such Plan Year pursuant to a Deferral Plan, minus (B) the amount actually allocated as a Company Stock Contribution to the account of the Participant under the RSP.

question: When are no credits made to a Participant’s RSP-Related Account under Section 5.2(b)(i)?
answer: No credits shall be made to a Participant’s RSP-Related Account pursuant to this Section 5.2(b)(i) for any pay period ending on or after July 1, 2007.

question: What is credited to a Participant’s RSP-Related Account under Section 5.2(b)(ii)?
answer: An amount equal to: (A) the Company Profit-Sharing Contribution percentage utilized for purposes of the RSP for that Plan Year.

question: What is the percentage of a Participant’s Compensation used to calculate the Company Stock Contribution?
answer: One percent

question: What is the calculation basis for the Company Stock Contribution, excluding the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation and Section 415 Limitations?
answer: The sum of (1) the Participant’s Compensation and (2) that portion of a Participant’s Compensation deferred during such Plan Year pursuant to a Deferral Plan

question: What is subtracted from the sum in the calculation of the Company Stock Contribution?
answer: The amount actually allocated as a Company Stock Contribution to the account of the Participant under the RSP

question: When are no credits made to a Participant’s RSP-Related Account pursuant to the Company Stock Contribution?
answer: For any pay period ending on or after July 1, 2007

question: What is the calculation basis for the Company Profit-Sharing Contribution?
answer: The Company Profit-Sharing Contribution percentage times the sum of (1) the Participant’s Compensation and (2) that portion of a Participant’s Compensation deferred during such Plan Year pursuant to a Deferral Plan

question: What is subtracted from the sum in the calculation of the Company Profit-Sharing Contribution?
answer: The amount actually allocated as a Company Profit-Sharing Contribution to the Account of the Participant under the RSP

question: What is the vesting rule for benefits credited under the Company Profit-Sharing Contribution at the time of a Supplemental Distribution?
answer: Benefits credited under this Section 5.2(b)(ii) at the time of a Supplemental Distribution shall be restricted to a Participant’s vested portion, as determined under the applicable provisions of the RSP

question: What happens to any non-vested portion of deferred compensation under the Company Profit-Sharing Contribution at the time of a Supplemental Distribution?
answer: Any non-vested portion of such deferred compensation to be paid shall be forfeited

question: What is the effective date for the Qualified Matching Contribution under the RSP?
answer: Effective with Compensation paid on or after January 1, 2017

question: What is the maximum percentage of a Participant’s Compensation eligible for a Matching Contribution under the RSP?
answer: Six percent of the Participant’s Compensation which is not counted under the RSP either because it is in excess of the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation for the Plan Year or because it has been deferred under a Deferral Plan

question: What compensation is excluded from the calculation of the Matching Contribution?
answer: Amounts paid prior to a Participant’s Entry Date under the RSP with respect to Qualified Matching Contributions

question: What is the vesting rule for Matching Contributions?
answer: The vesting of Matching Contributions will parallel the vesting rules applicable under the RSP

question: What is the calculation basis for the Company Conversion Contribution?
answer: The Company Conversion Contribution percentage times the sum of (a) the Participant’s Compensation and (b) that portion of a Participant’s Compensation deferred during such Plan Year pursuant to a Deferral Plan, minus the amount actually allocated as a Company Conversion Contribution to the Account of the Participant under the RSP

question: When are no Company Conversion Contributions made for employees in Band 50 and above?
answer: For periods after December 31, 2017

question: When are no Company Conversion Contributions made for employees below Band 50?
answer: For periods after December 31, 2018

question: Were any Company conversion contributions made for the pay period commencing March 30, 2009 through the pay period ending January 3, 2010?
answer: No

question: For which Participants did the limitation on Company conversion contributions not apply?
answer: Participants who were Retirement Eligible as of December 31, 2009

question: What was the amount of Company conversion contributions when they resumed after the pay period ending on January 3, 2010?
answer: Such contributions resumed in the same amount as in effect immediately prior to the pay period beginning on March 30, 2009

question: What is the calculation basis for the Transition Contributions for Former GE Capital Employees?
answer: The Transition Contribution percentage times the sum of (1) the Participant’s Compensation and (2) that portion of a Participant’s Compensation deferred during such Plan Year pursuant to a Deferral Plan, minus the amount actually allocated as a Transition Contribution to the Account of the Participant under the RSP

question: What happens if a participant would be eligible for both Company Conversion Contributions and Transition Contributions?
answer: Such individual shall only receive the greater of the Company Conversion Contributions and the Transition Contributions to which he or she would otherwise be entitled during such period of dual eligibility

question: When do Transition Contributions under Section 5.2(b)(v) expire?
answer: At the same time as the right to Transition Contributions under the RSP

question: When are no Transition Contributions made?
answer: For periods after March 31, 2011

question: Does the RSP provide for Disability Contributions?
answer: No

question: What is the additional amount credited to a Participant’s RSP-Related Account under Section 5.2(c)?
answer: 80 percent (or such lower percentage specified in the special agreement) of the Participant’s annual rate of base salary before any reduction for amounts deferred

question: When does the additional amount under Section 5.2(c) begin to be credited?
answer: For the period of January 1, 2008 and thereafter

question: What is the vesting period for amounts credited under Section 5.2(c)?
answer: Five-year vesting

question: What happens if a Participant’s service with the Company terminates before five years of actual service?
answer: Such amounts shall be forfeited by the Participant

question: When are amounts credited under Section 5.2(c) determined and credited?
answer: Amounts credited under this Section 5.2(c) shall be determined as of and credited on the one-year anniversary of the later of the date of the special agreement or the first day of the Participant’s employment by the Company

question: What is the time and manner for crediting amounts under Section 5.3?
answer: Amounts described in this Article 5 shall be credited to the Supplemental Account established for a Participant at such times and in such manner as may be determined by the Administrator

question: How are amounts credited to a Supplemental Account with respect to the application of the Section 415 Limitations determined?
answer: Amounts credited to a Supplemental Account with respect to the application of the Section 415 Limitations to the RP shall be estimated by the Administrator at the time of a Participant’s Separation from Service

question: When are amounts credited to a Supplemental Account pursuant to Section 5.2(c) credited?
answer: On the one-year anniversary of the later of the date of the special agreement or the first day of the Participant’s employment by the Company

question: To which subaccount are Company Stock Contributions initially credited?
answer: To a subaccount relating to the Stock Fund

question: To which subaccounts are other contributions credited?
answer: To the RSP-Related Account established for a Participant, which shall contain various subaccounts selected by the Administrator in its sole and exclusive discretion

question: What is the limit on amounts directed to the Stock Fund?
answer: Amounts may not be directed to the Stock Fund in excess of limits established by the Plan or Administrator pursuant to Article 7

question: What happens if amounts are directed to the Stock Fund in excess of the established limits?
answer: Any amounts directed to the Stock Fund in excess of those limits will be redirected in accordance with Article 7

question: Are subaccounts established under the Plan to coincide with self-directed brokerage accounts?
answer: No

question: What discretion does the Administrator have regarding additional book reserve accounts?
answer: The Administrator may, in its sole and exclusive discretion, establish additional book reserve accounts from time to time

question: What does the Administrator determine regarding increases, decreases, interest, dividends, and other income, gains and losses in book reserve accounts?
answer: The procedures to reflect and credit increases, decreases, interest, dividends, and other income, gains and losses shall be determined by the Administrator in its sole and exclusive discretion

question: What form are Supplemental Benefits payable under the Plan?
answer: In cash from the general assets of the Company

question: When may existing Participants make an initial Supplemental Election?
answer: On or before the date set by the Administrator, which shall not be later than December 31, 2005

question: When may Participants who have previously made an initial Supplemental Election change such election?
answer: On or before the date set by the Administrator, which shall not be later than December 31, 2005

question: When may employees who first become Participants after December 31, 2005 make an initial Supplemental Election?
answer: In accordance with rules and procedures adopted by the Administrator in compliance with Section 409A

question: What is the rule for a Participant’s initial Supplemental Election regarding Company contributions for the first, second, or third quarter of a calendar year?
answer: Such Participant’s initial Supplemental Election shall not be effective with respect to Company contributions calculated based on Compensation paid prior to the end of the first calendar year beginning on or after the date on which the Participant first is paid Compensation with respect to which Company contributions under this Plan are calculated

question: What is the rule for a Participant’s initial Supplemental Election regarding Company contributions for the fourth quarter of a calendar year?
answer: Such Participant’s initial Supplemental Election shall not be effective with respect to Company contributions calculated based on Compensation paid prior to the end of the second calendar year beginning on or after the date the Participant is first paid Compensation with respect to which Company contributions are calculated

question: What is the purpose of the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election?
answer: To determine which Supplemental Benefits are subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election

question: What happens if a Participant fails to satisfy the service requirement or make contributions required to receive Company Matching Contributions?
answer: It shall not impact the duration of the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election

question: What does the Company do with respect to Company contributions not covered by a Participant’s Supplemental Election?
answer: The Company shall be deemed to have made an Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election

question: Who is permitted to participate in open enrollment under Article 6?
answer: Employees eligible to participate in the Plan for a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits will be notified by Amex of their eligibility to participate for such Plan Year.

question: What is the condition for an employee to become eligible to participate in Deferral Benefits under the Plan effective January 1 of the following Plan Year?
answer: An Employee who was not otherwise eligible to participate in Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year and first satisfies the requirements for participation during one of the first three quarters of the Plan Year by reason of exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation will become eligible to participate in Deferral Benefits under the Plan effective January 1 of the following Plan Year.

question: What is the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date for an Employee who first satisfies the requirements for participation during the final calendar quarter of the Plan Year by reason of exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation?
answer: The first pay period beginning after the first day of the second month of the first calendar quarter of the following Plan Year.

question: What is the maximum percentage of Incentive Pay that may be elected to be deferred?
answer: The maximum percentage of Incentive Pay that may be elected is 85 percent.

question: What is the maximum amount that may be deferred from Base Salary and Incentive Pay under the Plan?
answer: The Administrator shall limit the amount that may be deferred from (A) Base Salary to be paid in the following Plan Year and (B) Incentive Pay to be paid in the second following Plan Year, to 100 percent of the Participant’s Base Salary rate in effect as of the December 31st of the Plan Year during which the Deferral Election is filed.

question: What is the condition for an employee to be considered eligible to participate in the Plan as of the date they first are employed in Band 50 or above?
answer: An Employee who is not already a Participant in the Plan shall be considered eligible to participate as of the date he or she first is employed in Band 50 or above.

question: What is the deadline for making a Deferral Election for a Plan Year?
answer: An eligible Employee for a Plan Year must make an irrevocable Deferral Election for the Plan Year on or before the December 15 of the preceding Plan Year, or if December 15 is on a weekend, the following Monday, or as of such other deadline as the Administrator may establish.

question: What is the form of a Deferral Election?
answer: A Deferral Election for a Plan Year shall be made in the manner and by the deadlines prescribed by the Administrator.

question: What is the requirement for a Deferral Election to be effective?
answer: All Deferral Elections will become irrevocable as of the day before the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date, or such earlier date as is established by the Administrator.

question: What is the condition for an employee to be permitted to file a mid-year Deferral Election?
answer: An Employee who is not already a Participant in the Plan and is not employed in Band 50 or above may make a mid-year Deferral Election if they first satisfy the requirements for participation during one of the first three quarters of the Plan Year by reason of exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation.

question: What is the condition for an employee to be treated as newly eligible to participate in the Plan under Section 6.3?
answer: An Employee who had previously been eligible to participate in an elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement (as defined for purposes of Section 409A) of Amex or its subsidiaries may be treated as newly eligible to participate and entitled to mid-year enrollment if (a) the Employee had received payment of all amounts under the Plan’s Deferral Account and any other elective account-balance plan and, as of the date of the last payment was not eligible to continue participation in the Plan’s Deferral Benefits or any other elective account-balance plan, disregarding for this purpose any right to delay payment; or (b) the Employee had ceased to be eligible to participate in Deferral Benefits under the Plan and all other elective account-balance plans and had not been eligible to participate in Deferral Benefits under the Plan or any other elective account-balance plan at any time during the 24-month period ending on the date the Employee again became eligible.

question: What is the maximum amount that may be deferred from Base Salary for an employee who becomes eligible to participate in the Plan by reason of being hired into or a promotion to Band 50 or above?
answer: The maximum amount that may be deferred from Base Salary is 100 percent of the Employee’s Base Salary rate in effect as of the date he or she becomes eligible to so participate.

question: What is the maximum amount that may be deferred from Base Salary for an employee who becomes eligible to participate in the Plan by reason of exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation?
answer: The maximum amount that may be deferred from Base Salary is 100 percent of the Employee’s Base Salary rate in effect as of the last day of the calendar quarter preceding the date he or she becomes eligible to so participate pursuant to Section 6.2(b).

question: What is the condition for an employee to have a special enrollment right under the Plan?
answer: An Employee does not have a special enrollment right merely because he or she exceeds the Section 415 limit under a Qualified Retirement Plan.

question: What is the date on which an employee exceeds the Section 401(a)(17) Limit?
answer: The date an Employee exceeds the Section 401(a)(17) Limit is determined based on Compensation for the Plan Year, regardless of whether some portion of that Compensation is excluded from Supplemental Benefits calculations because the Participant had not yet completed the service requirement for Company contributions.

question: What is the requirement for a Deferral Election to be made in accordance with Section 6.5?
answer: An eligible Employee for a Plan Year who wants to participate in the Plan with respect to Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year must make an irrevocable Deferral Election for the Plan Year on or before the December 15 of the preceding Plan Year, or if December 15 is on a weekend, the following Monday, or as of such other deadline as the Administrator may establish.

question: What is the condition for an employee to be eligible to participate in the Plan with respect to Deferral Benefits during a Plan Year?
answer: An employee who becomes eligible to participate in the Plan during a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits and who has not previously been eligible to participate in an elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement (as defined for purposes of Section 409A) of Amex or its subsidiaries may be offered by Amex the opportunity to participate in the Plan for the Plan Year in accordance with Section 6.2.

question: What is the condition for an employee to be permitted to make a mid-year Deferral Election under Section 6.2?
answer: An Employee who is not already a Participant in the Plan and is not employed in Band 50 or above may make a mid-year Deferral Election if they first satisfy the requirements for participation during one of the first three quarters of the Plan Year by reason of exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation.

question: What is the requirement for a Deferral Election to be limited to the amount of any payment otherwise payable in cash?
answer: All Deferral Elections shall be limited to the amount of any payment otherwise payable in cash, net of applicable withholdings.

question: What is the condition for an employee to be considered eligible to participate in the Plan as of the date they become eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan?
answer: An employee who was in Band 50 or above but not eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan shall be considered eligible as of the date the Employee (while still in Band 50 or above) becomes eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan.

question: What is the condition for an employee to be eligible to participate in the Plan with respect to Deferral Benefits during a Plan Year?
answer: An employee who becomes eligible to participate in the Plan during a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits and who has not previously been eligible to participate in an elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement (as defined for purposes of Section 409A) of Amex or its subsidiaries may be offered by Amex the opportunity to participate in the Plan for the Plan Year in accordance with Section 6.2.

question: What is the condition for an employee to be eligible to participate in the Plan with respect to Deferral Benefits after being rehired following a Separation from Service?
answer: With respect to an Employee who was a former Participant and again becomes a Participant after being rehired by the Company following his or her Separation from Service, the election rules in this Section shall apply to the Company Matching Contributions, Company Conversion Contributions and Company Profit-Sharing Contributions made to such Participant following his or her rehire date as if the rehire date (or if later, the resumption of eligibility to participate) were the date of initial participation eligibility.

question: What is the deadline for making an irrevocable Deferral Election for a Plan Year?
answer: The deadline for making an irrevocable Deferral Election for a Plan Year is December 15 of the preceding Plan Year, or if December 15 is on a weekend, the following Monday, or as of such other deadline as the Administrator may establish, but in all events prior to the beginning of such Plan Year.

question: What is the form of Deferral Election prescribed by the Administrator?
answer: A Deferral Election for a Plan Year shall be made in the manner and by the deadlines prescribed by the Administrator.

question: What must an Employee specify in their Deferral Election for a Plan Year?
answer: In his or her Deferral Election for a Plan Year, the Employee shall specify: (i) the items of his or her compensation eligible for deferral under Section 6.4(a) that the Employee wishes to defer for the Plan Year and the amount of each such item to be deferred, provided that the amount of all items to be deferred complies with Section 6.4(b) and any administrative limits imposed on elections made for such Plan Year; and (ii) in the case of an Employee in Band 50 or above as of the Band 50 Determination Date in the prior Plan Year, the time when his or her Deferral Benefits for such Plan Year shall be paid, which shall be either (A) the Separation from Service of the Participant, or (B) a specified date at least five years after the last day of the Plan Year at the time of the election; and the form of payment of his or her Deferral Benefits for the Plan Year, which shall be (A) a lump sum, or (B) five, ten or 15 substantially equal annual installments.

question: What happens if an Employee’s Deferral Election does not specify both a valid time of payment and a valid form of payment?
answer: Such Employee shall be deemed to have elected a lump-sum payment as of the January 1 or July 1 that is at least six months following his or her Separation from Service (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but in any event no later than 90 days).

question: Can an Employee who is not in Band 50 or above as of the Band 50 Determination Date file a special election regarding time and form of payment for Deferral Benefits?
answer: No, an Employee who is not in Band 50 or above as of the Band 50 Determination Date for the prior Plan Year may not file a special election regarding time and form of payment for Deferral Benefits.

question: What supplement applies to Deferral Benefits for an Employee not in Band 50 or above as of the Band 50 Determination Date?
answer: The Supplemental Election (without regard to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election) made pursuant to Section 5.4 will also apply to such Deferral Benefits.

question: Can a new Participant hired into or promoted to Band 50 participate in open enrollment for the following Plan Year?
answer: Yes, in the case of a new Participant who is enrolled as a result of being hired into or promoted to Band 50 (or transferring to eligible status while in Band 50 or above) after such date, the Administrator may permit such Employee to participate in open enrollment for the following Plan Year as a Band 50 or above Employee.

question: When is the Base Salary portion of a Participant’s Deferral Election withheld?
answer: The Base Salary portion of a Participant’s Deferral Election shall be withheld from each regularly scheduled Base Salary payroll.

question: When is the Incentive Pay portion of a Participant’s Deferral Election withheld?
answer: The Incentive Pay portion of a Participant’s Deferral Election shall be withheld at the time the Incentive Pay is or otherwise would be paid to the Participant.

question: What is the purpose of the Deferral Account established by the Administrator?
answer: The Administrator shall establish and maintain a Deferral Account with respect to each Participant’s Deferral Benefits. Amounts deferred by a Participant shall be credited to the Deferral Account established for the Participant at such times and in such manner as may be determined by the Administrator.

question: How are earnings credited to a Participant’s RP-Related Account?
answer: For each Participant, the RP-Related Account established pursuant to Section 5.1 shall be increased by the Imputed Earnings Credit (as such term is defined in the RP), not less frequently than annually, under procedures and at times determined by the Administrator and consistently applied for similarly situated Participants. Such earnings shall be credited at the same interest rate and computed in a similar manner (to the extent administratively feasible) as Imputed Earnings Credits are computed under the RP for each Plan Year.

question: How are earnings credited to a Participant’s RSP-Related Account?
answer: A Participant’s RSP-Related Account shall be credited with earnings under the Hypothetical Investment Method set forth below.

question: How are Deferral Benefits for Plan Year 2011 and later credited with earnings?
answer: For Plan Year 2011 and later, a Participant’s Deferral Benefits for such Plan Year shall be credited with earnings under the Hypothetical Investment Method set forth below.

question: How are Deferral Benefits for Plan Years prior to 2011 credited with earnings for Executive Officers?
answer: For Executive Officers, such Participant’s Deferral Benefits for Plan Years prior to 2011 shall be credited with earnings under the Hypothetical Investment Method set forth below effective for all earnings credited in any Plan Year beginning on or after January 1, 2011 and under the Interest Method set forth below for earnings credited in 2010 and prior Plan Years; provided, however, that earnings credited in 2010 (to the extent not paid out by October 27, 2010) will not exceed the AFR if Amex’s ROE is Below ROE Target Range; and provided further that for those Executive Officers who received payment in the 2010 Plan Year prior to October 27, 2010, earnings on the amounts paid prior to October 27, 2010 were calculated based on the Interest Method without reference to any AFR limitation.

question: How are Deferral Benefits for Plan Years prior to 2011 credited with earnings for Non-Executive Officers?
answer: For Non-Executive Officers, such Participant’s Deferral Benefits for Plan Years prior to 2011 shall be credited with earnings under the Interest Method set forth below through December 31, 2011; provided, however, that if a Participant becomes an Executive Officer during 2011, earnings for 2011 credited to such Participant’s Deferral Benefits for Plan Years prior to 2011 shall not exceed the AFR (except to the extent earnings in excess of the AFR have been paid out prior to the Participant’s becoming an Executive Officer). For 2012 and subsequent years, the Hypothetical Investment Method shall apply.

question: How are Deferral Benefits for Plan Years prior to 2011 credited with earnings for Retirees?
answer: For Retirees, such Participant’s Deferral Benefits for Plan Years prior to 2011 shall be credited with earnings under the Interest Method set forth below through December 31, 2012, and under the Hypothetical Investment Method set forth below effective January 1, 2013.

question: What is the Hypothetical Investment Method for credits to a Participant’s RSP-Related and Deferral Account?
answer: Credits to his or her RSP-Related and Deferral Account (to the extent subject to the Hypothetical Investment Method) shall be made to such subaccounts thereunder as directed by such Participant, using the subaccounts described in Section 5.3, provided, however, that with respect to Deferral Benefits attributable to Plan Years prior to 2011, the Participant may elect to have all or some of such Deferral Benefits invested in an investment option that credits earnings at the AFR instead of in the Stock Fund or the RSP-based investment options, and provided further that no Participant may transfer amounts to the subaccount representing the Stock Fund to the extent that such transfer would result in the aggregate Company Stock holdings of such Participant under the Plan exceeding ten percent of (i) the total value of his or her Deferral Account (determined at the time of the transfer) with respect to the investment of the Deferral Account or (ii) the total value of his or her RSP-Related Account (determined at the time of the transfer) with respect to the investment of the RSP-Related Account, nor may a Participant direct that more than ten percent of new contributions made to the RSP-Related Account or the Deferral Account, respectively, be directed to the subaccount representing the Stock Fund.

question: What is the default subaccount for a Participant who fails to designate one or more subaccounts under Section 7.4(c)?
answer: Such Participant shall be deemed to have selected a default account selected by the Administrator (which shall be deemed to be the subaccount representing the fund designated as the default fund under the RSP, unless the Administrator directs the use of a different fund).

question: What is the limit on the aggregate Company Stock holdings for a Participant under the Plan?
answer: No Participant may transfer amounts to the subaccount representing the Stock Fund to the extent that such transfer would result in the aggregate Company Stock holdings of such Participant under the Plan exceeding ten percent of (i) the total value of his or her Deferral Account (determined at the time of the transfer) with respect to the investment of the Deferral Account or (ii) the total value of his or her RSP-Related Account (determined at the time of the transfer) with respect to the investment of the RSP-Related Account.

question: What is the limit on new contributions directed to the subaccount representing the Stock Fund?
answer: No Participant may direct that more than ten percent of new contributions made to the RSP-Related Account or the Deferral Account, respectively, be directed to the subaccount representing the Stock Fund.

question: What happens if a Participant directs a transfer to the Stock Fund that would exceed the ten percent limit?
answer: If more than one subaccount is available, a Participant must designate, on a form or other medium acceptable to the Administrator, in one-percent increments, the amounts to be credited to each subaccount. A Participant shall be allowed to amend such designation consistent with the frequency of investment changes offered the Participant under rules governing the RSP for a given Plan Year, subject to any different or additional rules as may be established by the Administrator for this Plan. If a Participant has directed the transfer of amounts to the Stock Fund and the credits to the relevant Account of a Participant to the subaccount relating to the Stock Fund would result in the aggregate Company Stock holdings of such Participant under the Plan exceeding ten percent of the total value of such Account (determined at the time of the transfer) or has directed new contributions to an Account to the Stock Fund in an amount which would result in new contributions to such Account’s subaccount representing the Stock Fund exceeding ten percent of new contributions to such Account, then such Participant shall be deemed to have selected, with respect to any such excess, the default subaccount designated by the Administrator (which shall be deemed to be the subaccount representing the fund designated as the default fund under the RSP, unless the Administrator directs the use of a different fund).

question: What is the performance reflection for a Participant who elects to invest in the subaccount representing the Stock Fund?
answer: Subject to Section 7.4(d) and Section 7.6, the performance of the book reserve subaccount established for each Participant pursuant to Section 5.3 or Section 6.6 shall reflect the performance of the Stock Fund. Such subaccount shall reflect such increases or decreases in value from time to time, whether from dividends, gains, losses or otherwise, as may be experienced by the Stock Fund.

question: What is the performance reflection for a Participant who does not elect to invest in the subaccount representing the Stock Fund?
answer: To the extent the Participant does not elect (or is not permitted) to invest in the subaccount representing the Stock Fund, subject to Section 7.4(d), and to such rules as may be adopted by the Administrator, the performance of each book reserve subaccount established for each Participant shall reflect the performance of the investment fund that the Participant elects to have such subaccount represent. Each such subaccount shall reflect such increases or decreases in value from time to time, whether from dividends, gains, losses or otherwise, as that experienced by the related investment fund under the RSP or, in the case of the AFR investment option, as indicated by the AFR.

question: What is the interest rate used for crediting earnings under the Interest Method?
answer: Under the Interest Method, a Participant’s Deferral Account for a Plan Year shall be credited with interest equivalents each calendar year at the Schedule Rate in effect for the calendar year, subject to any limitations established under the Plan.

question: When do earnings on a Participant’s Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year under the Interest Method become 100 percent vested?
answer: Until January 1, 2011, with respect to amounts credited with earnings under the Interest Method, the earnings on a Participant’s Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year for a given calendar year at the Minimum Schedule Rate for the calendar year shall be 100 percent vested as such earnings are accrued and credited, and the portion of the earnings on a Participant’s Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year for a given calendar year at the applicable Schedule Rate in excess of the Minimum Schedule Rate for the calendar year, if any, shall become vested on the date that the Participant becomes Retirement Eligible, or upon the earlier death or Disability of the Participant, and thereafter as such earnings are accrued and credited. Effective December 31, 2010, all earnings amounts under the Interest Method with respect to Deferral Benefits not yet paid out shall be fully vested.

question: What is the vesting status of the principal amount in a Participant’s Deferral Account under the Interest Method?
answer: The principal amount of a Participant’s Deferral Account for a Plan Year shall be 100 percent vested at all times.

question: What is the vesting status of earnings in a Participant’s Deferral Account under the Interest Method before January 1, 2011?
answer: Until January 1, 2011, with respect to amounts credited with earnings under the Interest Method, the earnings on a Participant’s Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year for a given calendar year at the Minimum Schedule Rate for the calendar year shall be 100 percent vested as such earnings are accrued and credited, and the portion of the earnings on a Participant’s Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year for a given calendar year at the applicable Schedule Rate in excess of the Minimum Schedule Rate for the calendar year, if any, shall become vested on the date that the Participant becomes Retirement Eligible, or upon the earlier death or Disability of the Participant, and thereafter as such earnings are accrued and credited.

question: What is the vesting status of earnings in a Participant’s Deferral Account under the Interest Method after December 31, 2010?
answer: Effective December 31, 2010, all earnings amounts under the Interest Method with respect to Deferral Benefits not yet paid out shall be fully vested.

question: What are the special restrictions for Insiders regarding investment in the Stock Fund?
answer: Notwithstanding anything in the Plan to the contrary, (i) except as set forth below, credits to the Account of an Insider may not be made to a subaccount that reflects the performance of the Stock Fund, (ii) credits made to the Account of an Insider at any time may not be transferred to a subaccount that reflects the performance of the Stock Fund and (iii) credits made to an Insider’s Account at any time, and credits to a subaccount of an Insider that reflects the performance of the Stock Fund (which credits could only have been made when such individual was not an Insider) may not be transferred, withdrawn, paid out or otherwise changed, other than (A) pursuant to the Participant’s payment election or the rules governing distribution in the event of the Participant’s death (but only at such time as distribution is permitted under the securities rules, it being intended that a delay in the normal payment schedule occur only to the extent required by securities rules, as permitted by Section 409A) or (B) pursuant to applicable forfeiture provisions contained in the Plan.

question: When does the special restriction on Insiders apply?
answer: The provisions of this Section 7.6 shall apply to Insiders. Such provisions shall apply during all periods that such Participants are Insiders, including any period following cessation of Insider status during which such Participants are required to report transactions pursuant to Rule 16a-2(b) (or its successor) under the Exchange Act. This Section 7.6 shall be automatically applicable to any Participant who, on and after the date hereof, becomes an Insider. For purposes of the foregoing, the effective date of this Section 7.6 shall be the date the Participant becomes an Insider.

question: When does the special restriction on Insiders cease to apply?
answer: At such time as any Participant ceases to be an Insider (and any period contemplated by Rule 16a-2(b) has expired), this Section 7.6 shall cease to be applicable to such Participant.

question: What is the intent regarding the crediting of amounts to the accounts of Insiders that represents the performance of the Stock Fund?
answer: It is intended that the crediting of amounts to the accounts of Insiders that represents the performance of the Stock Fund is intended to qualify for exemption from Section 16 under Rule 16b-3(d) under the Exchange Act.

question: What is the rule for payment of Supplemental Benefits for a Participant who experiences a Separation from Service?
answer: Payment of Supplemental Benefits shall be made as follows: (i) if the governing Election calls for a lump-sum payment, it shall be made on the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’s Separation from Service for any reason (other than death or Disability) from the Company, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days; and (ii) if the governing Election calls for annual installment payments, they shall begin on July 1 of the calendar year following the Participant’s Separation from Service for any reason (other than death or Disability) from the Company, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each July 1 (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant.

question: What happens if a Participant continues receiving payments after re-employment?
answer: A Participant who has experienced a Separation from Service and is to receive or has begun receiving payments as set forth above, shall continue receiving any remaining payments according to the terms in effect on the date of his or her Separation from Service, even if later re-employed by the Company.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Separation from Service must be made if it is not due to death or Disability?
answer: The first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’s Separation from Service from the Company, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which annual installment payments for a Participant’s Separation from Service must begin if not due to death or Disability?
answer: On the first July 1 of the calendar year following the Participant’s Separation from Service from the Company, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Benefit under Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits must be made if the Participant has not had a Separation from Service, died, or incurred a Disability as of the specified date?
answer: On the first March 15 or September 15 following the specified date, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which annual installment payments for a Participant’s Deferral Benefit under Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits must begin if the Participant has not had a Separation from Service, died, or incurred a Disability as of the specified date?
answer: On the first March 15 or September 15 following the specified date, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Benefit under Post-2010 Deferral Benefits must be made if the Participant has not had a Separation from Service, died, or incurred a Disability as of the specified date?
answer: On the first January 1 or July 1 coinciding with or following the specified date, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which annual installment payments for a Participant’s Deferral Benefit under Post-2010 Deferral Benefits must begin if the Participant has not had a Separation from Service, died, or incurred a Disability as of the specified date?
answer: On the first January 1 or July 1 coinciding with or following the specified date, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Benefit under Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits must be made if the Participant has a Separation from Service and is Retirement Eligible?
answer: On the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the Participant’s Separation from Service from the Company, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Benefit under Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits must be made if the Participant has a Separation from Service and is not Retirement Eligible?
answer: On the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the Participant’s Separation from Service, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Benefit under Post-2010 Deferral Benefits must be made if the Participant has a Separation from Service and is Retirement Eligible?
answer: On the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’s Separation from Service from the Company, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which annual installment payments for a Participant’s Deferral Benefit under Post-2010 Deferral Benefits must begin if the Participant has a Separation from Service and is Retirement Eligible?
answer: On the first July 1 in the calendar year following the Participant’s Separation from Service from the Company, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Supplemental Account must be made upon the Participant’s death while still actively employed by the Company?
answer: On the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’s death, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Account must be made upon the Participant’s death while still actively employed by the Company?
answer: On the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the Participant’s death, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Account must be made upon the Participant’s death if the Participant elects annual installment payments and dies after such payments have commenced?
answer: On the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the Participant’s death, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Account must be made upon the Participant’s death if the Participant elects annual installment payments and dies after such payments have commenced under Post-2010 Deferral Benefits?
answer: On the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’s death, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Account must be made if the Participant dies after Separation from Service but before the six-month anniversary of Separation from Service?
answer: On the originally scheduled date.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Supplemental Account must be made if the Participant dies after Separation from Service but before the January 1 or July 1 (or other payment date within 90 days thereafter) that is six months after the Separation from Service?
answer: On the originally scheduled date.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Account must be made if the Participant’s payment had been delayed five years due to a modification of a Supplemental Election?
answer: In accordance with the death benefit provisions and will not wait for the five-year period to elapse.

question: What is the date on which a lump-sum payment for a Participant’s Deferral Account must be made if the Participant’s payment had been delayed five years due to a modification of a Supplemental Election applicable to Deferral Benefits?
answer: In accordance with the death benefit provisions and will not wait for the five-year period to elapse.

question: What is the condition under which a Participant’s Supplemental Benefits are limited to the Participant’s vested portion at the time of distribution?
answer: The payment of Supplemental Benefits to a Participant under this Section 8.1 shall be limited to a Participant’s vested portion of his or her Supplemental Account at the time of distribution.

question: What is the condition under which a Participant’s Deferral Account is limited to the Participant’s vested portion at the time of distribution?
answer: The payment of a Participant’s Deferral Account for a Plan Year under this Section 8.2 shall be limited to a Participant’s vested portion of his or her Deferral Account at the time of distribution.

question: What is the method for calculating each annual installment payment for a Participant who elected annual installment payments?
answer: Each annual installment payment shall be determined by multiplying the amount of the Participant’s Supplemental Benefits by a fraction, the numerator of which is one, and the denominator of which is the number of remaining payments.

question: What is the method for calculating each annual installment payment for a Participant who elected annual installment payments under a Deferral Election?
answer: Each annual installment payment shall be determined by multiplying the amount of the Deferral Benefits being paid pursuant to such Deferral Election by a fraction, the numerator of which is one, and the denominator of which is the number of remaining payments.

question: What is the effect of a Participant’s rehire during the five-year delay period for Supplemental Benefits?
answer: The rehire of a Participant during this intervening period will not affect the payment schedule.

question: What is the effect of a Participant’s rehire during the five-year delay period for Deferral Benefits?
answer: The rehire of a Participant during this intervening period will not affect the payment schedule.

question: What is the rule regarding the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and the five-year delay?
answer: The Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election may not be modified, and accordingly the portion of the benefit subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election will not be subject to any five-year delay.

question: What is the rule regarding the automatic revocation of a beneficiary designation in the event of divorce?
answer: Effective for Participants who die on or after January 1, 2013, if a Participant has designated his or her spouse as his or her beneficiary for either or both Accounts, that designation shall automatically become null and void in the event of the Participant’s divorce.

question: What is the rule regarding the payment of benefits if a beneficiary designation is voided due to divorce?
answer: The benefit shall be paid as if the former spouse had pre-deceased the Participant.

question: What is the rule regarding the payment of benefits if a beneficiary is divorced from the person named as beneficiary?
answer: These rules will also apply in the event a beneficiary is permitted to designate a beneficiary and becomes divorced from the person named as beneficiary.

question: What is the rule regarding liability for payment made to a named beneficiary prior to notification of divorce?
answer: Neither the Plan nor any other person will be liable for payment made to a named beneficiary prior to the date that the Plan is notified that such person is a divorced spouse.

question: What is the condition under which a Participant may revoke or modify a beneficiary designation?
answer: A Participant may revoke or modify such designation at any time by a further written designation in such form as the Administrator may prescribe.

question: What is the default beneficiary if no designation is in effect at the time Benefits become due?
answer: The Beneficiary of such Account shall be deemed to be the Participant’s surviving spouse, if any, and if not, the Participant’s estate.

question: What is the condition under which a Participant’s Beneficiary designation is automatically revoked?
answer: A Participant’s Beneficiary designation shall be deemed automatically revoked in the event of the death of the Beneficiary or, if the Beneficiary is the Participant’s spouse, in the event of dissolution of marriage.

question: A Participant dies after Separation from Service but before the January 1 or July 1 (or other payment date within 90 days thereafter) that is six months after the Separation from Service, payment in a lump sum shall be made to the beneficiary on the originally scheduled date?
answer: Payment in a lump sum shall be made to the beneficiary on the originally scheduled date.

question: To the extent however, that the Participant’s payment had been delayed five years due to his or her modification of a Supplemental Election that also applies to his or her Deferral Benefits, the Plan will make payment in accordance with the death benefit provisions and will not wait for the five-year period to elapse?
answer: The Plan will make payment in accordance with the death benefit provisions and will not wait for the five-year period to elapse.

question: In the event of the Disability of a Participant, payment of the Participant’s Supplemental Account shall be made as follows: if the governing Election calls for a lump-sum payment of his or her Supplemental Account, payment shall be made on the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days?
answer: Payment shall be made on the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: In the event of the Disability of a Participant, payment of the Participant’s Supplemental Account shall be made as follows: if the governing Election calls for annual installment payments of his or her Supplemental Account, payment shall begin on July 1 of the calendar year following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each July 1 (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant?
answer: Payment shall begin on July 1 of the calendar year following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each July 1 (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant.

question: In the event of the Disability of a Participant, payment of the Participant’s Deferral Benefits shall be made as follows: with respect to Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits, if the Participant elected a lump-sum payment of some or all of his or her Deferral Benefits, payment of such Deferral Benefits shall be made on the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days?
answer: Payment of such Deferral Benefits shall be made on the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: In the event of the Disability of a Participant, payment of the Participant’s Deferral Benefits shall be made as follows: with respect to Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits, if the Participant elected annual installment payments with respect to some or all of his or her Deferral Benefits, payment of such Deferral Benefits shall begin on the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each March 15 (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant for such Deferral Benefits?
answer: Payment shall begin on the first March 15 or September 15 which is at least six months following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each March 15 (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant for such Deferral Benefits.

question: In the event of the Disability of a Participant, payment of the Participant’s Deferral Benefits shall be made as follows: with respect to Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, if the Participant elected a lump-sum payment of some or all of his or her Deferral Benefits, payment of such Deferral Benefits shall be made on the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days?
answer: Payment of such Deferral Benefits shall be made on the first January 1 or July 1 which is at least six months following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: In the event of the Disability of a Participant, payment of the Participant’s Deferral Benefits shall be made as follows: with respect to Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, if the Participant elected annual installment payments with respect to some or all of his or her Deferral Benefits, payment of such Deferral Benefits shall begin on July 1 of the calendar year following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each July 1 (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant for such Deferral Benefits?
answer: Payment shall begin on July 1 of the calendar year following the Participant’s date of Disability, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days, and shall continue on each July 1 (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but in no event later than 90 days) thereafter for the period selected by the Participant for such Deferral Benefits.

question: If a Participant experiences an Unforeseeable Emergency, the Participant may petition the Administrator to receive a partial or full payout from the Plan?
answer: The Participant may petition the Administrator to receive a partial or full payout from the Plan.

question: The payout, if any, from the Plan shall not exceed the lesser of (a) the Participant’s vested Account balance, or (b) the amount necessary to satisfy the Unforeseeable Emergency, plus amounts necessary to pay federal, state, or local income taxes or penalties reasonably anticipated as a result of the distribution?
answer: The payout shall not exceed the lesser of (a) the Participant’s vested Account balance, or (b) the amount necessary to satisfy the Unforeseeable Emergency, plus amounts necessary to pay federal, state, or local income taxes or penalties reasonably anticipated as a result of the distribution.

question: A Participant shall not be eligible to receive a payout from the Plan to the extent that the Unforeseeable Emergency is or may be relieved (i) through reimbursement or compensation by insurance or otherwise, (ii) by liquidation of the Participant’s assets, to the extent the liquidation of such assets would not itself cause severe financial hardship or (iii) by cessation of a Deferral Election under this Plan?
answer: A Participant shall not be eligible to receive a payout from the Plan to the extent that the Unforeseeable Emergency is or may be relieved (i) through reimbursement or compensation by insurance or otherwise, (ii) by liquidation of the Participant’s assets, to the extent the liquidation of such assets would not itself cause severe financial hardship or (iii) by cessation of a Deferral Election under this Plan.

question: If the Administrator, in its sole discretion, approves a Participant’s petition for payout from the Plan, such payout shall be made in a lump sum on the date on which such approval occurs, or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but in no event later than 90 days?
answer: Such payout shall be made in a lump sum on the date on which such approval occurs, or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but in no event later than 90 days.

question: At the time of its determination, and to the extent permissible by Section 409A, the Administrator shall determine how any payment under this Section 8.6 will be applied against the Participant’s Account and the subaccounts thereunder?
answer: The Administrator shall determine how any payment under this Section 8.6 will be applied against the Participant’s Account and the subaccounts thereunder.

question: Notwithstanding anything in the Plan, the RP or the RSP to the contrary, to the maximum extent permitted by Section 409A and applicable law, any amount otherwise due or payable under the Plan may be forfeited, or its payment suspended, at the discretion of the Administrator, to apply toward or recover any claim the Company may have against the Participant, including but not limited to, for the enforcement of Amex’s Detrimental Conduct provisions under its long-term incentive award plan, to recover a debt to the Company or to recover a benefit overpayment under a Company benefit plan or program?
answer: Any amount otherwise due or payable under the Plan may be forfeited, or its payment suspended, at the discretion of the Administrator, to apply toward or recover any claim the Company may have against the Participant, including but not limited to, for the enforcement of Amex’s Detrimental Conduct provisions under its long-term incentive award plan, to recover a debt to the Company or to recover a benefit overpayment under a Company benefit plan or program.

question: No amounts shall be offset against a Participant’s Account prior to the date on which the offset amounts would otherwise be distributed to the Participant unless otherwise permitted by Section 409A?
answer: No amounts shall be offset against a Participant’s Account prior to the date on which the offset amounts would otherwise be distributed to the Participant unless otherwise permitted by Section 409A.

question: An offset shall be made only to the extent and in the manner permitted by the Section 409A Policy?
answer: An offset shall be made only to the extent and in the manner permitted by the Section 409A Policy.

question: The Company shall be entitled to deduct from any payment under the Plan, regardless of the form of such payment, the amount of all applicable income and employment taxes, if any, required by law to be withheld with respect to such payment or may require the Participant to pay to it such tax prior to and, to the extent permissible under Section 409A, as a condition of the making of such payment?
answer: The Company shall be entitled to deduct from any payment under the Plan, regardless of the form of such payment, the amount of all applicable income and employment taxes, if any, required by law to be withheld with respect to such payment or may require the Participant to pay to it such tax prior to and, to the extent permissible under Section 409A, as a condition of the making of such payment.

question: The Administrator may, in its sole discretion, make a mandatory lump sum pay-out of a Participant’s Account at any time, provided that such pay-out amount shall be in an amount equal to the lump sum value of such Account determined for the date of such pay-out?
answer: The Administrator may, in its sole discretion, make a mandatory lump sum pay-out of a Participant’s Account at any time, provided that such pay-out amount shall be in an amount equal to the lump sum value of such Account determined for the date of such pay-out.

question: Such pay-out (1) accompanies the termination and liquidation of the Participant’s entire interest under the Plan and all similar arrangements that constitute an account balance plan under Section 1.409A-1(c)(2) of the Treasury Regulations?
answer: Such pay-out (1) accompanies the termination and liquidation of the Participant’s entire interest under the Plan and all similar arrangements that constitute an account balance plan under Section 1.409A-1(c)(2) of the Treasury Regulations.

question: Such pay-out (2) the payment is not greater than the applicable dollar amount under Section 402(g)(1)(B) of the Code?
answer: Such pay-out (2) the payment is not greater than the applicable dollar amount under Section 402(g)(1)(B) of the Code.

question: “Change in Control” means the happening of any of the following: Any individual, entity or group (within the meaning of Section 13(d)(3) or 14(d)(2) of the Exchange Act) (a “Person”) becomes the beneficial owner (within the meaning of Rule 13d-3 promulgated under the Exchange Act) of 25 percent or more of either (i) the then outstanding common shares of Amex (the “Outstanding Company Common Shares”) or (ii) the combined voting power of the then outstanding voting securities of Amex entitled to vote generally in the election of directors (the “Outstanding Company Voting Securities”)?
answer: “Change in Control” means the happening of any of the following: Any individual, entity or group (within the meaning of Section 13(d)(3) or 14(d)(2) of the Exchange Act) (a “Person”) becomes the beneficial owner (within the meaning of Rule 13d-3 promulgated under the Exchange Act) of 25 percent or more of either (i) the then outstanding common shares of Amex (the “Outstanding Company Common Shares”) or (ii) the combined voting power of the then outstanding voting securities of Amex entitled to vote generally in the election of directors (the “Outstanding Company Voting Securities”).

question: Such beneficial ownership shall not constitute a Change in Control if it occurs as a result of any of the following acquisitions of securities: (A) any acquisition directly from Amex; (B) any acquisition by Amex or any corporation, partnership, trust or other entity controlled by Amex (a “Subsidiary”); (C) any acquisition by any employee benefit plan (or related trust) sponsored or maintained by Amex or any Subsidiary; (D) any acquisition by an underwriter temporarily holding Amex securities pursuant to an offering of such securities; (E) any acquisition by an individual, entity or group that is permitted to, and actually does, report its beneficial ownership on Schedule 13-G (or any successor schedule), provided that, if any such individual, entity or group subsequently becomes required to or does report its beneficial ownership on Schedule 13D (or any successor schedule), then, for purposes of this subsection, such individual, entity or group shall be deemed to have first acquired, on the first date on which such individual, entity or group becomes required to or does so report, beneficial ownership of all of the Outstanding Company Common Stock and Outstanding Company Voting Securities beneficially owned by it on such date; or (F) any acquisition by any corporation pursuant to a reorganization, merger or consolidation if, following such reorganization, merger or consolidation, the conditions described in clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) of Section 9.1(c) are satisfied?
answer: Such beneficial ownership shall not constitute a Change in Control if it occurs as a result of any of the following acquisitions of securities: (A) any acquisition directly from Amex; (B) any acquisition by Amex or any corporation, partnership, trust or other entity controlled by Amex (a “Subsidiary”); (C) any acquisition by any employee benefit plan (or related trust) sponsored or maintained by Amex or any Subsidiary; (D) any acquisition by an underwriter temporarily holding Amex securities pursuant to an offering of such securities; (E) any acquisition by an individual, entity or group that is permitted to, and actually does, report its beneficial ownership on Schedule 13-G (or any successor schedule), provided that, if any such individual, entity or group subsequently becomes required to or does report its beneficial ownership on Schedule 13D (or any successor schedule), then, for purposes of this subsection, such individual, entity or group shall be deemed to have first acquired, on the first date on which such individual, entity or group becomes required to or does so report, beneficial ownership of all of the Outstanding Company Common Stock and Outstanding Company Voting Securities beneficially owned by it on such date; or (F) any acquisition by any corporation pursuant to a reorganization, merger or consolidation if, following such reorganization, merger or consolidation, the conditions described in clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) of Section 9.1(c) are satisfied.

question: Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Change in Control shall not be deemed to occur solely because any Person (the “Subject Person”) became the beneficial owner of 25 percent or more of the Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities as a result of the acquisition of Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities by Amex which, by reducing the number of Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities, increases the proportional number of shares beneficially owned by the Subject Person; provided, that if a Change in Control would be deemed to have occurred (but for the operation of this sentence) as a result of the acquisition of Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities by Amex, and after such share acquisition by Amex, the Subject Person becomes the beneficial owner of any additional Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities which increases the percentage of the Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities beneficially owned by the Subject Person, then a Change in Control shall then be deemed to have occurred?
answer: Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Change in Control shall not be deemed to occur solely because any Person (the “Subject Person”) became the beneficial owner of 25 percent or more of the Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities as a result of the acquisition of Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities by Amex which, by reducing the number of Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities, increases the proportional number of shares beneficially owned by the Subject Person; provided, that if a Change in Control would be deemed to have occurred (but for the operation of this sentence) as a result of the acquisition of Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities by Amex, and after such share acquisition by Amex, the Subject Person becomes the beneficial owner of any additional Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities which increases the percentage of the Outstanding Company Common Shares or Outstanding Company Voting Securities beneficially owned by the Subject Person, then a Change in Control shall then be deemed to have occurred.
