question: What is the maximum period within which the Administrator shall reply to a claim filed under Section 10.1?
answer: 90 days of receipt, unless extended for reasonable cause

question: What is the maximum period within which the Administrator may extend the reply period for a claim under Section 10.2(a)?
answer: An additional 90 days for reasonable cause

question: What is the time limit for a claimant to request a review of an initial determination under Section 10.3(a)?
answer: Within 60 days after receipt of the written explanation

question: What is the time limit for a claimant to request a review of an initial determination under Section 10.3(b) for a disabled status claim?
answer: 180 days after receipt of the written explanation

question: What is the time limit for the Administrator to render a written decision on review under Section 10.4(a)?
answer: Normally within 60 days after receipt of the claimant’s request, or 120 days if extended

question: What is the time limit for the Administrator to render a written decision on review for a disabled status claim under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: Within 45 days, or 90 days if special circumstances require an extension

question: What is the time limit for the Administrator to render a decision on review for a disabled status claim if additional information is needed?
answer: The deadline will be tolled for the time period granted to the claimant to provide the information

question: What is the time limit for a claimant to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on review?
answer: The claimant’s right to bring such an action expires on the calendar date specified in Section 10.1(b)

question: What is the time limit for a claimant to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on appeal for a disabled status claim?
answer: The applicable limitations period under Section 10.1(b) applies, including the calendar date on which the right expires

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to provide access to documents and records relevant to a claim under Section 10.3 and 10.4?
answer: Reasonable access to and copies of any documents, records and other information relevant to the claim will be provided free of charge upon request

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to provide a written explanation when denying a claim under Section 10.2(a)?
answer: The reply shall include a written explanation using language calculated to be understood by the claimant, setting forth the specific reason or reasons for denial, the specific reference to relevant provisions of the Plan, additional material or information necessary to perfect the claim, steps to take if the claimant wishes to submit it for review, time limits for requesting a review, and the claimant’s right to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to provide a written explanation when denying a claim requiring a disabled status determination under Section 10.2(c)?
answer: The notice shall include a discussion of the decision, a copy of any internal rule, guideline, protocol or similar criterion relied upon, and an explanation of the scientific or clinical judgment for any medical necessity or experimental treatment exclusion or limit, or a statement that such explanation will be provided free of charge upon request

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure in a review of a disabled status claim under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: No deference shall be afforded to the prior determination, the persons who made the initial determination shall not be involved, and persons making the review decision shall not be subordinates of the original decision-makers

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to provide new or additional information to a claimant before a review decision under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The Administrator shall provide the new or additional evidence or rationale free of charge as soon as possible and sufficiently in advance of the deadline for the decision so that the claimant has a reasonable opportunity to respond

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to consult with health care professionals during a review of a disabled status claim under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The persons conducting the review shall consult with a health care professional of appropriate training and experience in the relevant field of medicine and shall identify any medical or vocational experts consulted to the claimant

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that no health care professional consulted in the review is a person who consulted in the original determination under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: No health care professional consulted in the course of the review shall be a person consulted in the course of the original determination (or a subordinate of such person)

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to provide a decision on review for a disabled status claim under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The decision shall be in writing, using language calculated to be understood by the claimant, and shall set forth the specific reason or reasons for denial, specific reference to relevant provisions of the Plan, the claimant’s right to access and copies of relevant documents, and the claimant’s right to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA

question: What is the requirement for all decisions on review under Section 10.4(c)?
answer: All decisions on review shall be final and shall bind all parties concerned to the maximum extent permitted by law

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to provide a discussion of the decision in a disabled status claim denial under Section 10.2(c) and 10.4(b)?
answer: The notice shall include a discussion of the decision, including an explanation of the basis for disagreeing with or not following the views presented by the claimant to the Administrator of health care professionals treating the claimant and vocational professionals who evaluated the claimant, the views of medical or vocational experts whose advice was obtained on behalf of the Plan, and a determination of disability by the Social Security Administration presented by the claimant

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to provide a statement regarding internal rules, guidelines, or protocols under Section 10.2(c) and 10.4(b)?
answer: The Administrator shall provide a copy of any internal rule, guideline, protocol or other similar criterion relied upon during the claims process or a statement that no such internal rules, guidelines, protocols or other similar criteria exist

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to provide an explanation of scientific or clinical judgment for a medical necessity or experimental treatment exclusion under Section 10.2(c) and 10.4(b)?
answer: The Administrator will provide an explanation of the scientific or clinical judgment for the determination (applying the terms of the Plan to the claimant’s medical circumstances) or a statement that such an explanation will be provided free of charge upon request

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that no new or additional information is considered without providing it to the claimant under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The Administrator shall not consider, generate or rely upon any new or additional information, or issue an appeal denial based on any new or additional rationale, without first providing the claimant, free of charge, with the new or additional evidence or rationale

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the persons making the review decision on a disabled status claim are not subordinates of the original decision-makers under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The persons who make the decision on review on behalf of the Administrator are not subordinates of the original decision-makers

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the persons conducting the review of a disabled status claim are not the same as those who made the original determination under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The persons who made the initial determination on behalf of the Administrator shall not be involved in the review

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to provide a written statement to a Participant regarding Payments reduction under Section 10.2(iii)?
answer: The Company shall provide to each Participant with respect to whom it is proposed that Payments be reduced, a written statement setting forth the manner in which the Total Payments in respect of such Participant were calculated and the basis for such calculations, including any opinions or other advice the Company has received from the Firm or other advisors or consultants

question: What is the requirement for the Firm to determine the value of non-cash benefits or deferred payments under Section 10.2(ii)(D)?
answer: The value of any non-cash benefits or any deferred payment or benefit shall be determined by the Firm in accordance with the principles of Sections 280G(d)(3) and (4) of the Code and regulations or other guidance thereunder

question: What is the requirement for the Firm to determine whether payments constitute parachute payments under Section 10.2(ii)(A)?
answer: All payments and benefits received or to be received by the Participant in connection with a Change in Control or termination of employment shall be treated as “parachute payments” unless, in the opinion of the Firm, such payments or benefits (in whole or in part) do not constitute parachute payments, including by reason of Section 280G(2)(A) or Section 280G(b)(4)(A) of the Code

question: What is the requirement for the Firm to determine whether a portion of Total Payments is subject to the Excise Tax under Section 10.2(ii)(C)?
answer: All “excess parachute payments” within the meaning of Section 280G(b)(2) of the Code shall be treated as subject to the Excise Tax unless, in the opinion of the Firm, such excess parachute payments (in whole or in part) represent reasonable compensation for services actually rendered (within the meaning of Section 280G(g)(4)(B) of the Code) in excess of the “base amount” (within the meaning of Section 280G(b)(3) of the Code) allocable to such reasonable compensation, or are otherwise not subject to the Excise Tax

question: What is the requirement for the Firm to determine the federal income tax rate for a Participant under Section 10.2(ii)?
answer: A Participant shall be deemed to pay federal income tax at the highest marginal rate of federal income taxation (and state and local income taxes at the highest marginal rate of taxation in the state and locality of such Participant’s residence, net of the maximum reduction in federal income taxes which could be obtained from deduction of such state and local taxes) in the calendar year in which the Payments are made

question: What is the requirement for the Company to pay the Firm for its services under Section 10.2(ii)?
answer: The Firm will be paid reasonable compensation by the Company for its services

question: What is the requirement for a Participant to elect in writing under Section 10.2(ii)?
answer: The Participant may elect in writing to have other components of his or her Total Payments reduced prior to any reduction in the Payments hereunder

question: What is the requirement for the Company to provide a written statement to a Participant regarding Payments reduction under Section 10.2(iii)?
answer: The Company shall provide to each Participant with respect to whom it is proposed that Payments be reduced, a written statement setting forth the manner in which the Total Payments in respect of such Participant were calculated and the basis for such calculations, including any opinions or other advice the Company has received from the Firm or other advisors or consultants

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to be the Plan’s agent for service of process under Section 10.1(b)?
answer: The Administrator shall be the Plan’s agent for service of process

question: What is the requirement for a claimant to exhaust remedies under the Plan’s claims procedures before seeking relief under Section 10.5?
answer: Any person requesting Benefits or wishing to assert a claim must exhaust all remedies under the Plan’s claims procedures before being entitled to seek relief under Section 10.5

question: What is the requirement for a cause of action to accrue under Section 10.1(b)?
answer: A cause of action is considered to have accrued when the person bringing the legal action knew, or in the exercise of reasonable diligence should have known, that a Plan party has clearly repudiated the claim or legal position which is the subject of the action

question: What is the requirement for a claimant to be barred and estopped from challenging a determination under Section 10.3(a)?
answer: If the claimant does not request a review of the initial determination within the 60-day period, the claimant shall be barred and estopped from challenging the determination

question: What is the requirement for a claimant to be barred and estopped from challenging a determination under Section 10.3(b)?
answer: If the claimant does not request a review of the initial determination within the 180-day period, the claimant shall be barred and estopped from challenging the determination

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that no deference is afforded to the prior determination in a disabled status claim review under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The Administrator shall ensure that no deference is afforded to the prior determination

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the persons making the review decision on a disabled status claim are not subordinates of the original decision-makers under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The persons who make the decision on review on behalf of the Administrator are not subordinates of the original decision-makers

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the persons conducting the review of a disabled status claim are not the same as those who made the original determination under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The persons who made the initial determination on behalf of the Administrator shall not be involved in the review

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that no new or additional information is considered without providing it to the claimant under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The Administrator shall not consider, generate or rely upon any new or additional information, or issue an appeal denial based on any new or additional rationale, without first providing the claimant, free of charge, with the new or additional evidence or rationale

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the persons conducting the review of a disabled status claim consult with a health care professional under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The persons conducting the review shall consult with a health care professional of appropriate training and experience in the relevant field of medicine and shall identify any medical or vocational experts consulted to the claimant

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that no health care professional consulted in the review is a person who consulted in the original determination under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: No health care professional consulted in the course of the review shall be a person consulted in the course of the original determination (or a subordinate of such person)

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the decision on review for a disabled status claim is provided within 45 days under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The decision shall be provided within 45 days (90 days, if the Administrator determines that special circumstances require an extension and so informs the claimant)

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the deadline for the Administrator’s response is tolled if additional information is needed under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The deadline for the Administrator’s response will be tolled for the time period granted to the claimant to provide the information (or the date that the claimant actually provides the information, if earlier)

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the decision on review for a disabled status claim is in writing and understandable under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The decision shall be in writing using language calculated to be understood by the claimant

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the claimant is entitled to receive reasonable access to and copies of all documents, records and other information relevant to the claim under Section 10.4(a)(iii)?
answer: The claimant is entitled, upon request and free of charge, to receive reasonable access to and copies of all documents, records and other information relevant to the claimant’s claim

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on review under Section 10.4(a)(iv)?
answer: The claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA now that the claim has been denied on appeal (subject to Section 10.5)

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on review for a disabled status claim under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA now that the claim has been denied on appeal (subject to Section 10.5) and, in the case of a decision regarding the Participant’s disabled status, the applicable limitations period under Section 10.1(b) applies

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on appeal under Section 10.1(b)?
answer: The claimant’s right to bring such an action expires on the calendar date specified in Section 10.1(b)

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on review under Section 10.4(a)?
answer: The claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA now that the claim has been denied on appeal (subject to Section 10.5)

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on review for a disabled status claim under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA now that the claim has been denied on appeal (subject to Section 10.5) and, in the case of a decision regarding the Participant’s disabled status, the applicable limitations period under Section 10.1(b) applies

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on appeal under Section 10.1(b)?
answer: The claimant’s right to bring such an action expires on the calendar date on which the claimant’s right to bring such an action expires

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on review under Section 10.4(a)?
answer: The claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA now that the claim has been denied on appeal (subject to Section 10.5)

question: What is the requirement for the Administrator to ensure that the claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA after a claim is denied on review for a disabled status claim under Section 10.4(b)?
answer: The claimant is entitled to bring an action under Section 502 of ERISA now that the claim has been denied on appeal (subject to Section 10.5) and, in the case of a decision regarding the Participant’s disabled status, the applicable limitations period under Section 10.1(b) applies

question: What is the governing law for the Plan?
answer: The Plan shall be construed in accordance with and governed by the laws of the State of New York to the extent not superseded by federal law, without reference to the principles of conflict of laws.

question: What is the standard of review required by ERISA for an arbitrator?
answer: The arbitrator shall defer to the factual findings and Plan interpretations of the Administrator unless such findings and interpretations are arbitrary and capricious.

question: What must a claimant provide if asserting entitlement to Benefits based upon facts not contained in the Plan’s records?
answer: Such person shall be required to provide satisfactory affirmative evidence of such facts.

question: What must a person provide if claiming entitlement to Benefits based upon service or compensation not reflected in the Plan’s records?
answer: Such person must provide satisfactory affirmative evidence of such service or compensation.

question: Who has sole and exclusive discretion to determine whether affirmative evidence is satisfactory?
answer: The Administrator shall have the sole and exclusive discretion to determine whether the above-referenced affirmative evidence is satisfactory.

question: What authority does the Administrator have with respect to matters under Article 10?
answer: The Administrator shall have the sole and exclusive authority with respect to any matter, action or decision under this Article 10, and the Committee shall have neither any authority with respect to such matters, nor the right or ability to limit or to interfere in any way with the Administrator’s authority with respect to such matters.

question: Can the Committee amend or terminate the Plan?
answer: The Committee or its delegate may, at any time, amend or terminate the Plan.

question: Can the Committee reduce or modify the amount of any Benefit payable to a Participant or Beneficiary at the time of Plan amendment or termination?
answer: The Committee may not reduce or modify the amount of any Benefit payable to a Participant or any Beneficiary receiving Benefit payments at the time the Plan is amended or terminated.

question: Can the Committee amend the definitions of Base Salary or Incentive Pay in a manner that would result in an impermissible alteration to an existing Deferral Election?
answer: The Committee shall not have the right to amend or modify the terms and provisions of the Plan to the extent such amendment or modification would result in a violation of Section 409A. In particular, amendments to the definitions of Base Salary or Incentive Pay hereunder shall not be made in a manner which would result in an impermissible alteration to an existing Deferral Election.

question: What happens to deferrals after Plan termination?
answer: No additional deferrals or contributions shall be credited to any Participant Account hereunder.

question: How are Participants’ Accounts paid following Plan termination?
answer: Participants’ Accounts shall be paid at such time and in such form as provided under Article 8.

question: Can the Committee distribute then existing Account balances after Plan termination?
answer: Either at the time of termination or on a subsequent date, the Committee may, in its discretion, determine to distribute the then existing Account balances of Participants and Beneficiaries.

question: Under what condition may the Committee distribute Account balances after Plan termination?
answer: The authority granted to the Committee under this Section 11.2 shall be implemented in compliance with the requirements of and only to the extent permissible under Section 409A.

question: Does the Plan create a trust or fiduciary relationship between the Company and the Participant?
answer: Nothing in the Plan shall create, or be construed to create, a trust of any kind or fiduciary relationship between the Company and the Participant, his or her designated Beneficiary, or any other person.

question: How are any rights to receive payments from the Company under the Plan construed?
answer: Any right to receive payments from the Company under the Plan shall be no greater than the right of any unsecured general creditor.

question: May the Company purchase securities or instruments to hedge its obligations under the Plan?
answer: The Company may, but need not, purchase any securities or instruments as a means of hedging its obligations to any Participant under the Plan.

question: Is the right to deferred compensation under the Plan transferable?
answer: The right of any Participant, or other person, to the payment of deferred compensation under the Plan shall not be assigned, transferred, pledged or encumbered except by the laws of descent and distribution.

question: Does participation in the Plan confer a right to continue in the employ of the Company?
answer: Participation in the Plan shall not be construed as conferring upon the Participant the right to continue in the employ of the Company as an executive or in any other capacity.

question: Does the Company reserve the right to dismiss any employee at any time?
answer: The Company expressly reserves the right to dismiss any employee at any time without liability for the effect such dismissal might have upon him or her hereunder.

question: Is deferred compensation under the Plan deemed salary or other compensation for the purpose of computing benefits under any plan or arrangement?
answer: Any deferred compensation payable under the Plan shall not be deemed salary or other compensation to the Participant for the purpose of computing the benefits under any plan or arrangement (including but not limited to any “employee benefit plan” under ERISA) except as expressly provided in such plan or arrangement.

question: Is the Plan intended to comply with Section 409A?
answer: The Plan is intended to comply with Section 409A, and shall be interpreted, operated and administered consistent with this intent and the Section 409A Policy.

question: What happens if the terms of the Plan fail to qualify for exemption from or to satisfy the requirements of Section 409A?
answer: To the extent the terms of the Plan fail to qualify for exemption from or to satisfy the requirements of Section 409A, the Plan may be operated in compliance with Section 409A pending amendment to the extent authorized by the Internal Revenue Service.

question: How is the Plan administered in compliance with Section 409A?
answer: In such circumstances, the Plan will be administered in a manner which adheres as closely as possible to its existing terms while complying with Section 409A.

question: Does the Company make any representations or warranties regarding tax consequences to a Participant under the Plan?
answer: The Company makes no representations or warranties and assumes no responsibility as to the tax consequences to any Participant who enters into a deferred compensation agreement with the Company pursuant to the Plan or any such Participant’s Beneficiary.

question: Is payment by the Company to a Participant or Beneficiary binding on all interested parties?
answer: Payment by the Company to the Participant (or to a Participant’s Beneficiary or Beneficiaries) in accordance with the terms of the Plan, including any designation of Beneficiary on file with the Administrator at the time of the Participant’s death, shall be binding on all interested parties and persons, including the Participant’s heirs, executors, administrators and assigns, and shall discharge the Company, its directors, officers and employees from all claims, demands, actions or causes of action of every kind arising out of or on account of the Participant’s participation in the Plan, known or unknown, for himself or herself, his or her heirs, executors, administrators and assigns.

question: Does any person connected with the Plan guarantee tax treatment for amounts deferred under the Plan?
answer: No person connected with the Plan in any capacity, including, but not limited to, the Company and its directors, officers, agents and employees, makes any representation, commitment, or guarantee that any tax treatment, including, but not limited to, Federal, state and local income, estate and gift tax treatment, will be applicable to any amounts deferred under the Plan, or paid to or for the benefit of a Participant or Beneficiary under the Plan, or that such tax treatment will apply to or be available to a Participant or Beneficiary on account of participation in the Plan.

question: Does any agreement executed pursuant to the Plan include the provisions of Section 12.6?
answer: Any agreement executed pursuant to the Plan shall be deemed to include the above provision of this Section 12.6.

question: Does the establishment of the Plan or any modification thereof give any Participant a legal or equitable right against the Company?
answer: Neither the establishment of the Plan nor any modification thereof, nor the creation of any account under the Plan, nor the payment of any benefits under the Plan shall be construed as giving to any Participant or other person any legal or equitable right against the Company, or any officer or employer thereof except as provided by law or by any Plan provision.

question: Does the Plan guarantee any Participant’s Account from loss or depreciation?
answer: No person (including the Company) in any way guarantees any Participant’s Account from loss or depreciation, whether caused by poor investment performance of a deemed investment or the inability to realize upon an investment due to an insolvency affecting an investment vehicle or any other reason.

question: Is the Company liable to any person on account of claims arising from the provisions of the Plan?
answer: In no event shall the Company or any successor, employee, officer, director or stockholder of the Company, be liable to any person on account of any claim arising by reason of the provisions of the Plan or of any instrument or instruments implementing its provisions (except that the Company shall make benefit payments in accordance with the terms of the Plan), or for the failure of any Participant, Beneficiary or other person to be entitled to any particular tax consequences with respect to the Plan, or any credit or distribution hereunder.

question: What happens if any provision of the Plan is held to be illegal or void?
answer: If any provision of the Plan is held to be illegal or void, such illegality or invalidity shall not affect the remaining provisions of the Plan, but shall be fully severable, and the Plan shall be construed and enforced as if said illegal or invalid provision had never been inserted herein.

question: Are the headings and captions in the Plan considered part of the Plan?
answer: The headings and captions herein are provided for reference and convenience only, shall not be considered part of the Plan, and shall not be considered in the construction of the Plan.

question: What is the Schedule Rate used to determine earnings credited on a Participant’s Deferral Accounts under the Interest Method?
answer: Under the Interest Method, the Schedule Rate used to determine the earnings credited on a Participant’s Deferral Accounts for such calendar year shall be determined under the following metric, based on Amex’s “ROE” for such calendar year and its “ROE Target Range” for such calendar year: Amex’s ROE Schedule Rate.

question: What is the Schedule Rate if Amex’s ROE is below the ROE Target Range?
answer: Below ROE Target Range Moody’s A Rate.

question: What is the Schedule Rate if Amex’s ROE is within the ROE Target Range?
answer: Within ROE Target Range 9%.

question: What is the Schedule Rate if Amex’s ROE is above the ROE Target Range?
answer: Above ROE Target Range 11%.

question: What does Amex’s “ROE” for a calendar year mean?
answer: Amex’s “ROE” for a calendar year means Amex’s consolidated annual return on equity for such calendar year, as reported by Amex, subject to adjustment for significant accounting changes as determined by the Committee in its sole discretion.

question: What does Amex’s “ROE Target Range” for a calendar year mean?
answer: Amex’s “ROE Target Range” for a calendar year means the ROE target range announced by Amex and in effect on January 1st of such calendar year.

question: Can the Committee change the Schedule Rate for any calendar year?
answer: Except as otherwise provided by Section 9.2(b)(ii) of the Plan, the Schedule Rate under this Schedule A for any calendar year may be changed by the Committee, prospectively or retrospectively, in its sole discretion, without prior notice to or consent of Participants or Beneficiaries.

question: What is the definition of “grandfathered” status for pre-2008 deferral plans?
answer: Principal for years up to and including 2004 is considered grandfathered, as is interest for years prior to 1999, and interest in the 1999-2004 years to the extent that the Participant was Retirement Eligible by December 31, 2004.

question: Are interest amounts for 1999-2004 deferral plans considered grandfathered for Participants not Retirement Eligible by December 31, 2004?
answer: Interest for the 1999-2004 Deferral Plans for Participants who were not Retirement Eligible by December 31, 2004 is never considered grandfathered, regardless of whether it exceeded the minimum interest crediting amount for the year.

question: Does “grandfathered” status have a practical impact?
answer: “Grandfathered” status does not have a practical impact except in the case of an employee who receives severance payments from the Company.

question: What does a reference to “termination of employment” refer to for non-grandfathered benefits?
answer: References to “termination of employment” or similar concepts refer to “Separation from Service” for non-grandfathered benefits.

question: Which plan document controls for grandfathered benefits?
answer: For grandfathered benefits, the definition in effect under the prior plan document will control.

question: Are the rules governing pre-2008 deferral plans reflected in Article 8 of the Plan?
answer: The rules governing these benefits are NOT reflected in Article 8 of the Plan, which addresses only Deferral Plan benefits from 2008-2010 (as “Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits”) and current Deferral Plan benefits (as “Post-2010 Deferral Benefits”).

question: What happens if a Participant elected a specified date and is still active on that date?
answer: If the Participant elected a specified date AND is still active on the specified date, the Participant will be paid according to specified date election.

question: What happens if a Participant elected a lump sum and is still active on the specified date?
answer: If lump sum elected, paid in a lump sum on the first March 15/September 15 on/following the elected date.

question: What happens if a Participant elected installments and is still active on the specified date?
answer: If installments elected, payments begin on the first March 15/September 15 on/following elected date, with subsequent installments paid on each March 15.

question: What happens if a Participant terminates during payment and is not Retirement Eligible upon termination?
answer: If termination occurs during payment, and the Participant is not Retirement Eligible upon termination, the remainder of the installments are paid in a lump sum on the first March 15/Sept 15 that is at least 6 months following termination.

question: What happens if a Participant is Retirement Eligible at the time of termination and elected a specified date?
answer: If the Participant is Retirement Eligible at the time of termination, the Participant will be paid according to elections.

question: What happens if a Participant elected a lump sum and is Retirement Eligible at termination?
answer: If lump sum elected, paid in a lump sum on the first March 15/September 15 on/following the specified date (even if later than termination of employment).

question: What happens if a Participant elected installments and is Retirement Eligible at termination?
answer: If installments elected, payments begin on the first March 15/September 15 on/following elected date (even if later than termination of employment), subsequent installments will be paid on each March 15.

question: Can the commencement of payments occur after retirement?
answer: Commencement could be AFTER retirement. (This is different from the rule for current Deferral Plan benefits.)

question: What happens if a Participant was not Retirement Eligible upon termination and terminates before the specified date?
answer: If a Participant was not Retirement Eligible upon termination, and terminates from employment before the specified date, the Participant is paid in a lump sum on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following termination.

question: What happens if a Participant goes out on severance?
answer: If the Participant is going out on severance, see Severance Flow Chart and follow questions. Severance may delay start of any payments based on termination of employment/retirement for GRANDFATHERED amounts, since it may delay deemed termination of employment.

question: What happens if a Participant elected to be paid at retirement and is Retirement Eligible upon termination?
answer: If the Participant is Retirement Eligible upon termination, the Participant will be paid according to elections.

question: What happens if a Participant elected a lump sum and is Retirement Eligible upon retirement?
answer: If lump sum elected, paid in a lump sum on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following retirement.

question: What happens if a Participant elected installments and is Retirement Eligible upon retirement?
answer: If installments elected, payments begin on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following retirement; subsequent installments will be paid on each March 15.

question: What happens if a Participant is not Retirement Eligible upon termination and goes out on severance?
answer: If not Retirement Eligible upon termination, paid in a lump sum on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following termination.

question: What happens if a Participant leaves the Company as a result of Disability?
answer: The Participant will be paid according to elections.

question: What happens if a Participant elected a lump sum and leaves due to Disability?
answer: If lump sum elected, paid in a lump sum on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following date of disability.

question: What happens if a Participant elected installments and leaves due to Disability?
answer: If installments elected, payments begin on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following date of disability; subsequent installments will be paid on each March 15.

question: What happens if a Participant dies before payments begin or before receiving all installments?
answer: The balance of the Participant’s account will be paid as a lump sum to the Participant’s designated beneficiary on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following date of death.

question: What is the definition of “Retirement Eligible”?
answer: “Retirement Eligible” means that the Participant is at least age 55 AND has at least 10 years of service.

question: Are the rules governing 2008-2010 plans subject to Section 409A of the Code?
answer: These plans do not include any “grandfathered” money and are subject to Section 409A of the Code in their entirety.

question: What is the termination date of the Plan for Publishing Participants?
answer: The Plan is hereby irrevocably terminated, effective as of and contingent on the closing of the transactions described in the Purchase and Sale Agreement by and between American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. and a subsidiary of Time Inc. (the “Termination Date”), solely with respect to the Participants in the Plan who are employees of American Express Publishing Corporation on the Termination Date (“Publishing Participants”).

question: What is the date by which all crediting of Plan accounts of Publishing Participants shall cease?
answer: As of the Termination Date, all crediting of Plan accounts of Publishing Participants shall cease.

question: When will the benefits to each Publishing Participant be paid after the Termination Date?
answer: Each Publishing Participant’s remaining accrued and unpaid benefits shall be paid to such participant in accordance with the requirements of Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B) and on a date within twelve months of the Termination Date.

question: What determines the benefit to be paid to each Publishing Participant?
answer: The benefit to be paid to each Publishing Participant shall be determined in accordance with the Plan’s provisions.

question: What section of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, must all benefits under the Plan comply with?
answer: All benefits under the Plan shall be paid only in a manner that complies with the requirements of Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

question: What is the purpose of Schedule E in the Plan?
answer: Effective upon the establishment of the proposed joint venture involving the Global Business Travel business (as it may be defined in one or more documents governing the joint venture) (the “Business”), this Schedule shall govern Plan participation by individuals who are Participants in this Plan and who as of or after the establishment of the Business are or become employees of one or more entities forming part of the Business under circumstances in which the documents governing the Business obligate the Business to provide such individuals with benefits comparable to those offered by the Company for some period of time (a “Business Employee”).

question: What happens if there is a conflict between Schedule E and other provisions of the Plan?
answer: In the event of any conflict between this Schedule E and other provisions of the Plan, this Schedule shall control for Business Employees; provided, however, that nothing in this Schedule shall affect the time of payment, form of payment or amount of benefits accrued prior to the date this Schedule becomes applicable to a Participant, or the Participant’s other rights and obligations with respect to such benefits.

question: What is the condition for a Business Employee to continue to participate in the Plan?
answer: A Business Employee may continue to participate in this Plan during such period as may be established under the documents governing the Business as the period during which the Business Employee will receive benefits comparable to those offered by the Company.

question: What must a Business Employee have done to be entitled to participate in the Plan?
answer: A Business Employee must have been a Participant in the Plan immediately prior to the establishment of the Business (or, if later, the date the employee became a Business Employee) (in either case, the Business Employee’s “Transition Date”), or must have been offered the opportunity to enroll prior to his or her Transition Date and must either have enrolled in the Plan prior to the Transition Date or after the Transition Date but prior to the enrollment deadline that would have applied if the Business Employee had remained an Employee of the Company.

question: What discretion does the Administrator retain regarding continued participation?
answer: The Administrator retains the discretion to decline to permit continued participation by any Business Employee, so long as such exclusion does not cause a violation of Section 409A.

question: When does a Business Employee’s ability to continue to make and receive contributions under the Plan terminate?
answer: A Business Employee’s ability to continue to make and receive contributions under the Plan will terminate as of the earlier of: (a) The date the Business Employee has a Separation from Service from the Business (or such later date as is required by Section 409A), provided that an individual who is rehired prior to termination of participation under paragraph (b) below may resume participation in accordance with the terms of the Plan, this Schedule and Section 409A; (b) The later of the following dates (which dates and hence the applicable time of termination of participation may differ for different types of contributions): (i) The end of the period during which comparable benefits are required under the documents governing the Business; or (ii) The date cessation of contributions is permissible under Section 409A.

question: What happens when a Business Employee again becomes an Employee of the Company?
answer: An individual who was a Business Employee but who again becomes an Employee of the Company will cease to have participation in the Plan governed by this Schedule, except for benefits attributable to his or her time as a Business Employee, and provided that this change in status will not invalidate any elections filed as a Business Employee.

question: How are Deferral Benefits deducted from a Business Employee’s compensation?
answer: Deferral Benefits will be deducted from each participating Business Employee’s Base Salary and Incentive Pay in accordance with the Business Employee’s timely filed Deferral Election and the following rules.

question: What constitutes “Base Salary” for a Business Employee under the Plan?
answer: The term “Base Salary” shall be deemed to include amounts paid by the Business that correspond on the relevant payroll system to amounts which would be “Base Salary” if paid by the Company to an Employee, determined in compliance with applicable law.

question: What constitutes “Incentive Pay” for a Business Employee under the Plan?
answer: The term “Incentive Pay” shall be deemed to include amounts paid by the Business that correspond on the relevant payroll system to amounts which would be “Incentive Pay” if paid by the Company to an Employee, determined in compliance with applicable law.

question: How are Deferral Elections treated when a Business Employee reaches the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation?
answer: For purposes of determining whether any Deferral Election that takes effect after the Participant reaches the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation has been activated, compensation from the Company and the Business will be aggregated unless otherwise required by law.

question: Are Deferral Elections filed prior to becoming a Business Employee affected by a change in status?
answer: A Business Employee’s Deferral Elections filed prior to the individual’s becoming a Business Employee shall not be affected by the individual’s change in status to a Business Employee.

question: Can a Business Employee file a new Deferral Election after participation ceases?
answer: A Business Employee may not file a new Deferral Election after his or her participation ceases in accordance with Article 1 of this Schedule (without prejudice to the Business Employee’s rights under Article 1 of this Schedule to resume participation and file any appropriate Deferral Elections upon qualifying to do so again).

question: How are Supplemental Benefits allocated to a Business Employee’s RSP-Related Account?
answer: Supplemental Benefits may be allocated to a Business Employee’s RSP-Related Account in such amounts as Amex may determine, in its sole discretion.

question: What is expressly authorized for Amex in calculating Supplemental Benefits?
answer: Without limiting Amex’s discretion under the foregoing, Amex is expressly authorized to take into account amounts paid by the Business when calculating Supplemental Benefits for a Business Employee attributable to periods after the establishment of the Business.

question: What is the nature of benefits under the Plan in terms of funding?
answer: Benefits under the Plan shall at all times be unfunded obligations of the Company.

question: What right does the Company retain regarding payments to the Business?
answer: Without prejudice to the Company’s right to require the Business to provide it (or any rabbi trust established under the Plan) with such payments as may be agreed between the Company and the Business from time to time.

question: What does the agreement between the Company and the Business not give to the Plan, Participant, or Beneficiary?
answer: No such agreement may give the Plan, any Participant or any Beneficiary a right to any such funds or to payment of Plan benefits in preference to the general creditors of the Business.

question: What remains subject to the claims of general creditors of the Business?
answer: Any amounts paid to the Company (or any rabbi trust established under the Plan) by the Business with respect to the Plan shall remain subject to the claims of the general creditors of the Business to the extent necessary to preserve the unfunded nature of the Plan.

question: How is vesting of benefits determined for a Business Employee?
answer: Vesting of benefits shall be determined in the same fashion as if employment with the Business were employment with the Company, and the vesting of contributions shall be accelerated to the extent the vesting of similar contributions is accelerated under the RSP with respect to Business Employees; provided, however, that with respect to Company contributions attributable to employment with the Business, the normal vesting schedule applicable to comparable contributions under the Business’ 401(k) plan shall apply and vesting will not be accelerated.

question: How are credits to a Participant’s Deferral Account and RSP-Related Account made during employment as a Business Employee?
answer: Credits to a Participant’s Deferral Account and RSP-Related Account with respect to benefits earned while a Business Employee shall be made in accordance with Article 7 of the Plan.

question: How is the time and form of payment determined for a Business Employee?
answer: The time and form of payment for a Business Employee shall be determined as if employment with the Business were employment with the Company, and a Participant shall not experience a Separation from Service merely on account of employment with the Business instead of the Company, unless otherwise provided by Section 409A.

question: When does a Participant not experience a Separation from Service due to employment with the Business?
answer: A Participant shall not be treated as commencing a new period of participation in the Plan merely because of employment with the Business instead of the Company, although a Participant who Separates from Service from the Business and subsequently is rehired shall be subject to the normal rules for rehires (as expressly modified by this Schedule E, if applicable to the Participant upon rehire).

question: How is a Separation from Service determined for a Business Employee?
answer: Once a Participant becomes a Business Employee, the occurrence of a Separation from Service shall be determined by treating the Business (along with any affiliates of the Business treated as a single employer with the Business under Section 414(b) or (c) of the Code, using the 80 percent common ownership standard) as the “service recipient.”

question: What happens if a Participant again becomes an Employee of the Company after being a Business Employee?
answer: If the Participant subsequently again becomes an Employee of the Company, benefits attributable to the Participant’s reemployment by the Company shall be governed by the Plan’s normal rules regarding Separation from Service, but benefits attributable to periods during and prior to the Participant’s employment as a Business Employee shall continue to be governed by this Section.

question: How is a Participant’s designation of a Beneficiary affected by becoming a Business Employee?
answer: A Participant’s designation of a Beneficiary will not be affected merely because the Participant becomes a Business Employee.

question: What right does the Committee retain regarding this Schedule or any other part of the Plan?
answer: The Committee reserves the right to amend or terminate this Schedule or any other part of the Plan at any time, without the approval of any individual (including Business Employees), subject to compliance with Section 409A.

question: What does nothing in this Schedule give to any Business Employee or individual?
answer: Nothing in this Schedule gives any Business Employee or any other individual a right to payment of benefits superior to that of any other Participant or Beneficiary under the Plan, or the right to be hired by or remain in the employ of the Company, the Business or any affiliate of either.

question: What does nothing in the Plan or this Schedule create?
answer: Nothing in the Plan or this Schedule is intended to create any third-party beneficiary rights under the documents governing the establishment of the Business.

question: What right does the Administrator have regarding the interpretation of this Schedule?
answer: The Administrator shall have the right to construe, interpret and administer this Schedule to the same extent as the rest of the Plan, and to decide any claims arising from this Schedule pursuant to the Plan’s normal claims process.

question: What does this Schedule constitute?
answer: This Schedule constitutes part of the Plan and shall at all times be interpreted in a manner compliant with Section 409A.
